home.title: Birb Learn
home.description: A free, open-source platform for studying school subjects, starting with mathematics.
home.heroTitle: Study with clarity, practice with confidence.
home.heroSubtitle: Step-by-step lessons, interactive simulators, solved exercises and mock exams with annotated answers. All free, in Portuguese, English and Spanish.

features.title: Everything you need to really learn
features.subtitle: Each lesson combines theory, intuition and practice, so you understand the why and don't just memorize the formula.

lessons.title: Guided lessons
lessons.text: Content organized in short learning paths, from the basics to advanced topics, with progress tracking.

simulators.title: Interactive simulators
simulators.text: Explore concepts hands-on: tweak parameters, watch the graph react and build intuition.

solved.title: Solved exercises
solved.text: Problems with step-by-step solutions so you can check your reasoning after trying on your own.

simulado.title: Custom mock exams
simulado.text: Build exams by topic and difficulty and get every question graded with a full explanation.

themes.title: Your way
themes.text: Four themes, light and dark mode and three languages, so you can study comfortably at any hour.

openSource.title: Open and free
openSource.text: No ads, no sign-up. The source code is public and anyone can contribute.

disciplines.title: Choose where to start

learn.title: Learn at your pace
learn.text: Read the lessons, explore the simulators and track your progress.

practice.title: Test what you learned
practice.text: Take a mock exam and see the annotated solution for every question.

physics.kineticGraphLabel: Graph of kinetic energy versus speed
physics.workDiagramLabel: Block pushed by a force across a rough floor
physics.stopsEarly: Friction wins: the block stops after {distance} m, before covering the chosen distance.
physics.workTheoremNote: Work–energy theorem: final KE = initial KE + total work (g = {g} m/s²).
physics.trackLabel: Ball rolling down a valley-shaped track
physics.trackStopped: The ball has stopped: all the remaining mechanical energy was dissipated by friction (mostly into thermal energy).
physics.trackNote: Without friction, mechanical energy stays constant and the ball returns to its starting height. With friction, part of it is dissipated (g = {g} m/s²).
physics.springGraphLabel: Graph of the spring force versus deformation
physics.springCompressed: Compressed spring: it pushes the block back toward x = 0. The shaded area of the graph is the stored energy.
physics.springStretched: Stretched spring: it pulls the block back toward x = 0. The shaded area of the graph is the stored energy.
physics.springRelaxed: Spring at its natural length: with no deformation there is no force and no elastic energy.
physics.orbitLabel: Elliptical orbit of a planet around a star
physics.showEqualAreas: Show {count} areas swept in equal times
physics.orbitNote: Orbit around the Sun: with a in astronomical units (AU) and T in years, T² = a³. Each colored slice is swept in the same time interval and all have the same area.
physics.forceRatio: Force compared with the original scenario
physics.gravitationNote: The two forces always have the same magnitude and opposite directions (action and reaction). Doubling the distance divides the force by 4.

presets.earthPerson: Earth and a 70 kg person on its surface

physics.gravityGraphLabel: Graph of gravitational acceleration versus altitude
physics.gravityNote: Equatorial radius used: {radius} km. The calculation uses g = GM/R² and leaves out the effect of rotation.
